body.statement: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\). With probability at least \(1-\delta\), \(h_{G,e}\) is not the zero polynomial and \(\mathcal E_{G,e}\) is proper. For every complex covariance specialization \(\Sigma\notin\mathcal E_{G,e}\) in the model image, \[\{z\in\mathbb C:p_e(\Sigma,z)=0\}=\mathcal Z_e(G,\Sigma).\] This equality uses the specialized prime incidence ideal \(I_G\) and remains valid when its full \(\Lambda\)-fiber is positive dimensional. The circuits in \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\) certify that every coordinate-preserving slice meets every generic finite branch, intermediate poles and identically zero-over-zero components are retained or lifted back to \(I_G\), the specialized leading coefficient does not drop, and no finite root is exchanged with a root at projective infinity. The roots are distinct whenever the squarefreeness circuit is nonzero.
body.justification: The exceptional set makes the word generic auditable and excludes poles, lost leading terms, and infinity components explicitly.
body.gap: Generic RUR specialization theory supplies general bad loci, but no existing result packages \(S_G\)-localization of the prime SEM incidence ideal and single-edge projection into a causal graph certificate.
body.consumer: Users can test whether an observed or simulated covariance lies inside the certified operating region before interpreting polynomial roots.
